per_plume.source_hint: lee-side / wake orographic cloud band extending WNW from Hawai'i Island; vog-cloud mix not fully excluded
evidence: Narrow bright white linear feature 408 km long, almost entirely over ocean (land_frac 0.017, only small overlap with Hawai'i, no island swallowed), behavior typical of a cloud/wake band rather than surface smoke. [E5, E3]

No FIRMS fire clusters, ruling against wildfire_smoke. Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, ruling against vog_mauna_loa. Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE erupting unknown with strong glow/flames and 76 summit thermal pixels, so Kilauea degassing possible but not confirmed as a strong vog source. [E2, E6]

Measured drift toward 288 deg at ~40.9 km/h (fit R2 0.65) with inferred source end on west side of Hawai'i Island (19.855,-155.135, 52.3 km from Kilauea, 65.1 km from Mauna Loa). Wind at that source end from 144 deg (toward 324 deg) agrees within ~36 deg, supporting WNW transport from the island. [E4, E7]

Wind at centroid from 229 deg (toward 49 deg) disagrees with drift toward 288 deg by ~120 deg, and using that wind puts the upwind end 299 km from Kilauea and 265 km from Mauna Loa. Disagreement shows heterogeneous flow and must lower confidence. [E1, E4, E8]

Bright white color and very narrow linear morphology attached to the island cloud mass but offset 52-65 km from the summits favors condensation in a lee/wake cloud band over pure vog, which is typically more diffuse bluish haze anchored at the vent. [E4, E3]

evidence_cited.text: Narrow bright white linear feature 408 km long, almost entirely over ocean (land_frac 0.017, only small overlap with Hawai'i, no island swallowed), behavior typical of a cloud/wake band rather than surface smoke.

No FIRMS fire clusters, ruling against wildfire_smoke. Mauna Loa NORMAL/GREEN not erupting, ruling against vog_mauna_loa. Kilauea WATCH/ORANGE erupting unknown with strong glow/flames and 76 summit thermal pixels, so Kilauea degassing possible but not confirmed as a strong vog source.

Measured drift toward 288 deg at ~40.9 km/h (fit R2 0.65) with inferred source end on west side of Hawai'i Island (19.855,-155.135, 52.3 km from Kilauea, 65.1 km from Mauna Loa). Wind at that source end from 144 deg (toward 324 deg) agrees within ~36 deg, supporting WNW transport from the island.

Wind at centroid from 229 deg (toward 49 deg) disagrees with drift toward 288 deg by ~120 deg, and using that wind puts the upwind end 299 km from Kilauea and 265 km from Mauna Loa. Disagreement shows heterogeneous flow and must lower confidence.

Bright white color and very narrow linear morphology attached to the island cloud mass but offset 52-65 km from the summits favors condensation in a lee/wake cloud band over pure vog, which is typically more diffuse bluish haze anchored at the vent.

classify.caveats: Wind field is spatially variable: SE flow at the island supports WNW transport but SW flow at the centroid disagrees strongly with measured drift, so transport is uncertain. Kilauea was in unrest (WATCH/ORANGE with summit thermal) so a vog component mixed with cloud cannot be fully excluded from true-color alone.

kilauea.activity_summary: No overflows or spattering at north or south vents over the past day; strong glow and flames continue. No reactivation of intrusion emplaced two nights ago. Earthquake activity continues underneath Halemaʻumaʻu.

mauna_loa.activity_summary: Mauna Loa earthquake counts decreased in September compared to August, and minor inflation continues. Mauna Loa had a decrease in seismic activity compared to the previous month; a total of 53 earthquakes were detected in Mauna Loa's summit region during the September reporting period, after 87 in August. Most earthquakes occurred deep beneath the upper Southwest Rift Zone or broadly scattered around the upper flanks.
